record.tranche_reason: Compares adaptive and non-adaptive optimizers on few-shot image-classification accuracy, a different setting from the optimizer comparisons in V4.
record.gate_note: Figure 3 and Section 3.7 report test accuracy by optimizer. The text gives a qualitative comparison, while the plotted values are figure-only. Results for other claim versions are not reported as tests.
record.test_reason: The study compares adaptive and nonadaptive optimizers using held-out image-classification accuracy in a new setting: few-shot fine-tuning of pretrained ResNet-18 networks. Section 3.7 explicitly relates this comparison to Wilson et al.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the optimizer conclusion: adaptive optimizers can improve few-shot fine-tuning test accuracy, especially with the normalized classifier. The paper also concludes that low learning rates stabilize adaptation and that updating the entire network helps under large domain shifts.
record.recipe_differences: Few-shot fine-tuning of pretrained feature extractors on novel classes; compares seven optimizers and reports novel-class accuracy. It does not compare training and test error or use the original claim's settings.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported optimizer advantage is especially pronounced with the normalized classifier.
record.problems: The optimizer comparison is reported in a figure without numeric values or uncertainty in the supplied text. The experiment is a few-shot adaptation setting and does not report training performance alongside test accuracy.
record.rows_left_out: Other results do not measure a claim version. Figure 3 does not provide recoverable numeric optimizer values, so only the stated qualitative comparison is recorded.

record.verdict_notes: The reversal is qualitative and concerns the reported optimizer-group comparison; it does not establish that every adaptive optimizer beats every nonadaptive optimizer. V4 says adaptive methods often perform worse, so these few-shot results qualify its scope rather than refute that frequency claim.
